The paper presents an adjoint-based sampling method for electromagnetic scattering from perfectly conducting objects.
The method does not require explicit knowledge of the Green's function for the background medium.
It allows simultaneous sampling for all points and dipole directions.
The approach is based on solutions to certain adjoint problems involving divergence-free tangential current sources.
The adjoint sampling method can be interpreted as a nonlinear backprojection algorithm.
The method alleviates limitations of standard sampling methods that require multiple forward solves.
Numerical experiments illustrate the efficiency and accuracy of the adjoint approach.
The framework is applicable to a wide class of inverse problems beyond electromagnetic scattering.
The method computes integrals over several directions without separate computations for each.
The adjoint problem formulation enables efficient evaluation of sampling functions.
The paper discusses the relation between the adjoint sampling method and standard backprojection algorithms.
The method provides additional quantitative information usually missing in standard sampling methods.
The approach reduces computational cost by avoiding explicit Green's function calculations.
The method is suitable for time harmonic electromagnetic wave scattering problems.
The adjoint method integrates well with existing linear sampling and backprojection techniques.
